places.name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, this ancient rock fortress features frescoes, water gardens, and breathtaking views from the summit.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited early morning to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Wear sturdy shoes for the climb and carry water.

places.name: Lion’s Paw Staircase & Frescoes
places.ai_summary: An iconic feature of Sigiriya, this staircase with lion's paw carvings leads up to the fortress, accompanied by ancient frescoes.

places.place_tip: Look for the ancient graffiti on the Mirror Wall.

places.name: Pidurangala Rock Hike (Sunrise View)
places.ai_summary: A popular hiking spot offering panoramic views of Sigiriya Rock and the surrounding landscapes, especially stunning at sunrise.

opening_hours.notes: Bring a flashlight if hiking before sunrise.

attribution.title: Ibban Katuwa, Sri Lanka 0021
attribution.author: Michael Gunther
attribution.description:
Cist Burials at Ibban Katuwa, Sri Lanka.

Early Iron Age people buried their dead in lidded chambers called cists, that were constructed from slabs of stone. These are secondary burials. The body would first be buried in soil, and allowed to decay naturally until only its skeleton remained; its bones would then be collected and reburied in a pot within the cist, along with a variety of grave goods such as food, beads, and weapons.

The burials at any given location, such as this one, would typically belong to a single family group (lineage). A lineage symbol is often carved onto the capstones.

places.name: Sigiriya Lake Walk
places.ai_summary: A scenic walk around the lake at the base of Sigiriya Rock, offering beautiful views and a chance to see local wildlife.

opening_hours.notes: Early morning or late afternoon is best for wildlife spotting.

places.place_tip: Bring binoculars for birdwatching and a camera for photos.

attribution.title: Jetwing Vil Uyana
attribution.author: Rohan Kar
attribution.description:
A ‘back to nature’ retreat in a man-made private nature reserve aptly describes Jetwing Vil Uyana, an eco-friendly resort in an area of remarkable beauty. Here tranquillity is guaranteed alongside wonderful service, great food, Ayurveda & spa and view of the Sigiriya rock fortress.
Possibly the only hotel in the world built over reed beds and paddy fields purposely created on reclaimed agricultural land. Accommodation is in thatched cabanas, many with their own pools, over water, marsh land, paddy fields or within the forest. Explore the grounds via wooden walkways or take a boat or ferry in search of rare birds and wildlife.
